pageCache.pageTitle: Our Vision and Values | All Souls C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
All Souls C of E Primary School
OUR VISION AND VALUES
Experiencing life in all its fullness, we grow to be the best that we can be.
Whenever we ask the children what they love about our school, their answers highlight many of the different aspects what life at All Souls entails. They spoke of their teachers, friends, topics, trips – we could go on!
In the Bible, we read these words that Jesus spoke:
The thief comes only in order to steal, kill and destroy. I [Jesus] have come in order that you might have life – life in all its fullness. (John 10:10)
It is this promise of Jesus – a promise of life in all its fullness – that we have taken hold of as an expression of what we seek to offer at All Souls. We want everyone who is part of our school community – children and adults – to experience life in the fullest sense of the word. But what does that actually look like?
At All Souls, it means that we value each person as the individual God made them to be; we encourage creativity and teamwork; we forgive quickly and put others’ needs before our own; we actively work to care for creation; we learn the full range of subjects (including Religious Education) and aim high with our learning. It also means that we value our daily Collective Worships as spaces to ask big questions, reflect on what is happening in the world around us and pray. Put simply, we are a school that is life-giving.
This is the heart of what being part of All Souls is about and our school vision simply reflects that. As we experience life in all its fullness in this way, we can be confident that we are growing to be the best that we can be.
Our school vision is supported by our four core Christian values. For everyone to experience life in all its fullness and grow to be the best that we can be, we need:
Please click on each value above to find out more information.
WISDOM to find our way through life
COMPASSION to love those living alongside us
PERSEVERANCE to overcome the challenges we face
All Souls C of E Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome | All Souls C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
All Souls C of E Primary School
WELCOME
A very warm welcome to All Souls CE Primary School
Welcome to All Souls CE Primary School — a truly special place in the heart of Fitzrovia and London’s West End.
At All Souls, every child is known, valued, and nurtured. We are a thriving, caring, and ambitious community where children flourish both academically and personally. Our dedicated and passionate staff inspire a lifelong love of learning, helping every child to grow in confidence, curiosity, and creativity.
We are proud to serve our local and wider community, welcoming children of all faiths and none. Our school family reflects the wonderful diversity of central London, and together we learn, celebrate, and grow in an atmosphere built on respect, compassion, and thankfulness. As a Church of England school, our Christian vision underpins everything we do. Guided by our faith and the teachings of Jesus, we aim for every child to experience life in all its fullness - to make wise choices, be happy, be kind, and persevere in all that they do. We want every child to be the very best they can be.
We are extremely proud of our outstanding academic and pastoral outcomes and of The Village - our excellent specialist provision for autistic children, which is a vibrant and inclusive part of our school community. Our central London location offers incredible opportunities for our pupils to explore and learn from the city’s rich cultural, historical, and artistic life.
Through our broad and balanced curriculum, as well as our excellent wraparound care, we open doors to the world around us and encourage our pupils to dream big and believe in themselves.
If you are considering All Souls for your child, I warmly invite you to visit us and experience the warmth, energy, and joy of our school for yourself. Please contact the Head of School through the school office at office@allsoulsprimary.co.uk.
We look forward to welcoming you into our All Souls family.
All Souls C of E Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: Links With Our Parish | All Souls C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
All Souls C of E Primary School
LINKS WITH OUR PARISH
As a Church of England school, we have close links with our parish church: All Souls Langham Place.
Every Friday, a member of the church’s Children’s Team, comes to lead our Collective Worship in school. Additionally, a leader of the church’s Sunday group for children with additional needs regularly visits The Village to tell a Bible story to our Village children.
We hold whole-school services at the church four times a year for Harvest, Christmas, Easter and our Year 6 Leavers’ Service. On special occasions, such as at Christmas, the school choir sing at a Sunday service at the church.
We are very grateful that Jamie Sperling – Music Lead (0-18s) and Prom Praise for Schools Associate Music Director leads our school choir, alongside Mrs Legg.
A number of our governors are regular attenders of All Souls Church.
We are very proud of the fact that our recent SIAMS inspection (2023) highlighted our partnership with our parish as a strength of the school. The report commented that: Well-established partnerships enhance and affirm provision, particularly with diocese and church. Both involve giving as well as receiving ‘life in all its fullness’.
You can find out more about All Souls Langham Place here: www.allsouls.org
The best day of my working week is Thursday, as that's the day I come over from All Souls to co-lead the choir with Mrs Legg in the afternoon after school.
We spend our time learning fun warm-ups and singing new songs. The children respond so positively to it and it's a joy to sing with them, as they prepare for singing at the whole-school services for the important Christian events of the year.
Music Lead (0-18) at All Souls Church
All Souls Parish, Langham Place
All Souls C of E Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND | All Souls C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
All Souls C of E Primary School
SEND
Our SENDCo is Kate McCarter
At All Souls we believe that every child has the ability to achieve and find success during their time with us. We aim to establish pupils' strengths and educational needs as soon as they start school and, in this way, develop programmes of support that will help all of our pupils achieve their potential in their future.
Special Educational Provision means different or additional support other than that which is generally made for children of the same age. Each class teacher adapts their teaching to meet the needs of each pupil. However, some children need more specialised support or intervention.
Please click here to find out about 'The Village', our specialist ASD provision.
If you have any enquiries, please email our Interim SENDCo, Eirini Lymperi via elymperi@allsoulsprimary.co.uk.
SEN Information Report
PUPILS WITH DISABILITIES
At All Souls we believe that all pupils regardless of race, gender or disabilities should have equal access to the curriculum in order to achieve to their highest potential. Currently, the SENCO, class teacher and learning support assistants collaborate in order to provide resources and support that will enable pupils with a learning disability to participate fully in the school curriculum. For more information, please refer to the school's Special Educational Needs Policy.
Whilst our school is built over a number of floors, we do have a disabled access and disabled toilet. For more information please refer to the school’s Disability and Access Policy.
Withdrawal groups have proven to be very successful in enabling access to the curriculum in Literacy and Numeracy. The school provides intervention in the form of Catch Up and Five Minute box Literacy and Numeracy support, which provides individual support by trained Teaching Assistants. Additional support is positively enjoyed by pupils and valued by parents as an additional learning opportunity for their children. Additional intervention is also provided depending on the needs of pupils. Pupil Premium funding is used to provide much of this intervention.
To see the Westminster Local Offer for SEND, please click on the link: https://www.westminster.gov.uk/local-offer
To find independent, impartial and confidential advice regarding your child with special needs and/or a disability, please contact:
Westminster Information Advice Support Service: Home (westminsteriass.co.uk)
iass@westminster.gov.uk
Camden SENDIASS: Home (sendiasscamden.co.uk)
SENDIASS@camden.gov.uk

HOME LEARNING
Each class receives homework on a Friday and it is due back on a Wednesday morning (Monday morning for Butterflies in the EYFS).

Wrap Around Care
We offer wrap around care for children aged 5 to 11 each day from 7.50am to 5.30pm

All Souls C of E Primary School
Wrap Around Care and Enrichment Clubs
We provide wrap around care each day from 7.50am to 5.30pm.
At breakfast club, your child will have the opportunity to a light nutritious breakfast as well as taking part in some quiet games, crafts or reading.
Breakfast club places can be booked in person with Suhad (playworker) by calling in at the Riding House Hall on Riding House Street between 7.50am and 9am Monday to Friday. The charge is £5 per session.
After School Wrap Around Care
After school wrap around care is in additional to our enrichment clubs. After school wrap around care is hosted in the Riding House Hall site. Children are collected by the wrap around care staff and taken to the hall.
Our wrap around care provider is Kids Adventure Days and provides the ideal childcare solution for busy families. Adventure Days offer your child a range of activities from sports to crafts and from Lego club to cookery. Please click on the website link below to book or find out more information.
https://www.kidsadventuredays.com/clubs
Wrap around care is booked using the link above and costs £6 per hour.
Here at All Souls we also offer a range of enrichment clubs. These take place on the school site and are run by a mixture of school staff or external providers. Places at these clubs are offered to children at the start of each main term or in the case of choir at the start of the school year.
All Souls C of E Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: School Ambassadors | All Souls C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
All Souls C of E Primary School
SCHOOL AMBASSADORS
Every year at All Souls, we invite the children in Year 6 to apply to become a School Ambassador. The job of the ambassadors is to represent the school in a variety of circumstances, including showing visitors around the building, welcoming people to school events and overseeing attendance awards. Most importantly they are regarded as role models for the rest of the school to follow and be inspired by.
This is seen as a highly prestigious and important role to undertake, and as part of the application process the children are required to make a formal presentation to an interview panel of school leaders and governors to show case their communication skills.
Each term, a selection of ambassadors are chosen to lead the school.
Meet the School Ambassadors of 2025-2026
Here are our School Ambassadors for Summer 2026
All Souls C of E Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: Young Sports Leaders | All Souls C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
All Souls C of E Primary School
YOUNG SPORTS LEADERS
At All Souls, we have Year 6 Young Sports Leaders as part of our PE provision, who regularly meet with the PE Lead to discuss any ideas regarding physical education. Young Sports leaders have an opportunity to share their own thoughts and opinions with the PE Lead and collectively agree on any decisions that are made.
Young Sports Leaders apply at the start of each academic year by writing a letter of application stating why they think they would make an excellent candidate for the job and most importantly, why they want to be one!
Once applications are received, the Young Sports Leaders are trained to lead activities and games with younger children and are taught the important qualities that are needed when working with young people. After passing their First Aid Training, and YSL assessment, they will sign a contract and receive their red t-shirts. The Young Sports Leaders will then be able to work with Key Stage 1 children, during lunchtimes, to lead games and ensure playtimes are inclusive for everyone, and that no child is left alone with no one to play with. This role develops our core values of wisdom, compassion, perseverance and compassion, as well as building their confidence and communication skills throughout the year.
Sports Leaders also help to organise and lead events such as Sports Day and intra-school competitions.
Meet the Young Sports Leaders of 2025-2026 - coming soon
All Souls C of E Primary School
